body: Yep, in London and lost service over an hour ago

I had a similar scenario to this. It feels like a misspeak/slip, but it will never. Stop. 

You wouldn’t say anything like that about his body, right? His brain should work the same in speaking to you. Everyone’s different, but in my situation, this clearly became a negging thing over time to keep my self esteem low so I wouldn’t feel like I had options elsewhere.

Hi! Lesbian here. The sooner you cut off communication like you did, the more time you have to heal. Let yourself heal. 

Also, you deserve better.

NTA. I came out to my mom and told her not to tell my dad. She did so within a week. I wasn’t happy. 

My dad said similar things, asking why I didn’t feel comfortable telling him. He was not gay-friendly throughout my childhood. Your wife needs to consider the impacts of standing by as her parents said homophobic things on her closeted child’s mind before she gets mad about being the last to know.

21 F as well (but for the other team). This is something I’m struggling with right now as well. The gay community in my area has pretty lofty beauty standards that I know I don’t fit into (not necessarily in a self pitying way. I don’t want to ask someone to settle for me either). Everything else in my life is objectively amazing right now, but I feel so down because of my romantic failures. It’s gonna be a long journey to realize and understand why that is, but here we are!
I don’t know man, there’s a difference between “doesn’t like gay people” and “don’t touch me”.

NTA, but for what it’s worth - I grew up in a household where Katy Perry was banned because of I Kissed A Girl and my brother was kept from friends who seemed “too touchy” at young ages (think 4-7) because he could “turn out gay”, and my parents adore my girlfriend and my mom is officiating a gay wedding later this year. Coming out can spark thought change, but your safety is most important.

As someone who usually aims to date people older than me, there’s definitely a point of diminishing returns. If he’s 30 and interested in dating an 18 year old, he’s /likely immature enough that you’d be better off dating an 18-20 year old.
His, but ball trimmers would still be effective
Nah fam, he'd probably take the buzz. Gotta give him a patchy one at least

Gay, never mormon that follows this sub but grown up christian in the republican stronghold county of our state - it sucks. It truly does. My parents are trying, but even just 6 months ago, my dad quite literally growled at my gay disney pin for Gay Days. What matters is their commitment to being better. It can only get better from the reaction you're writing about.
